Every element — from pressing for ZTE relief to offering only limited, reversible concessions — serves China's strategic position.

recommendation_rationale: This was clearly the right call for China in early May 2018. The May 3-4 Beijing talks did produce an agreement to keep talking, and China's strategy of negotiating while avoiding escalation was exactly what it pursued — and it worked to buy time through mid-2018 before the tariff war escalated further. The recommendation correctly identified that a full trade war would hurt China more given its chip dependency, that the ZTE crisis was an acute vulnerability requiring diplomatic engagement, and that Made in China 2025 was a non-negotiable red line. China's actual approach in this period closely matched this recommendation, and it preserved maximum flexibility.
lookahead_bias_rationale: All cited sources are dated before the decision date (April 3, April 4, April 16 events, and May 2 web search results). The reasoning is grounded in point-in-time facts and reasonable strategic assessment. No future knowledge is evident.
